words.enDefinition: Study of limits, derivatives, and integrals for functions of one variable

examples.en: Our single-variable calculus course begins with the idea of approaching a point along a curve.
examples.zh: 我们的「一元微积分」课从沿曲线趋近某点的概念讲起。

examples.en: We used single-variable calculus to find when the height of the ball stopped increasing.
examples.zh: 我们用「一元微积分」求球的高度在什么时候停止增加。

words.enDefinition: Rule assigning one output to each allowed input drawn from a single variable

examples.en: The example models water temperature as a function of one variable, with time as the input.
examples.zh: 示例把水温表示为「一元函数」，以时间为输入。

examples.en: We graphed a function of one variable before examining how quickly its values changed near zero.
examples.zh: 研究其函数值在零附近的变化速度之前，我们先画出了这个「一元函数」的图像。

collocations: graph a function of one variable
differentiate a function of one variable
evaluate a function of one variable

words.enDefinition: Set of real numbers strictly between its two designated endpoints

examples.en: The open interval contains the points between the endpoints but excludes the endpoints themselves.
examples.zh: 「开区间」包含两个端点之间的点，端点本身不包括在内。

examples.en: We checked the derivative on the open interval before discussing the boundary points.
examples.zh: 我们先检查了「开区间」上的导数，再讨论边界点。

words.enDefinition: Set of real numbers between two endpoints including the endpoints themselves

examples.en: On a closed interval, the endpoint values count when we compare possible maxima.
examples.zh: 在「闭区间」上比较可能的最大值时，端点的函数值也需要纳入。

examples.en: The tutor chose a closed interval so that we would include both endpoint values.
examples.zh: 老师换成了「闭区间」，这样两个端点的值也都包括在内。

collocations: restrict a function to a closed interval

words.enDefinition: Interval contained between some finite lower and upper real numbers

examples.en: The graph shows a bounded interval even though neither endpoint is included in the domain.
examples.zh: 图像表示的是一个「有界区间」，尽管两个端点都不在定义域内。

examples.en: The exercise first restricts the formula to a bounded interval before comparing its values.
examples.zh: 习题先把公式的适用范围限定为一个「有界区间」，再比较函数值。

collocations: restrict the domain to a bounded interval

words.enDefinition: Value the outputs approach as the input approaches a specified point

examples.en: We estimated the limit of a function from values on either side of the marked point.
examples.zh: 我们根据标记点两侧的函数值估算了「函数的极限」。

examples.en: The limit of a function can exist even if the formula is undefined at that point.
examples.zh: 即使公式在该点无定义，「函数的极限」也可以存在。

collocations: find the limit of a function
evaluate the limit of a function
existence of the limit of a function

words.enDefinition: Get arbitrarily close to a specified number as the input changes

examples.en: On both sides of the open circle, the function values approach a value.
examples.zh: 在空心圆的两侧，函数值都「趋近某个值」。

examples.en: The outputs seem to approach a value as the inputs get closer to zero.
examples.zh: 随着输入接近零，输出似乎「趋近某个值」。

words.enDefinition: Convergence of function values to a real number at the approach point

examples.en: The graph has a finite limit even though the marked point is missing.
examples.zh: 虽然标记点缺失，图中函数仍有「有限极限」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks whether the function has a finite limit near the vertical line.
examples.zh: 习题问这个函数在竖线附近是否有「有限极限」。

words.enDefinition: Value approached when inputs come toward a point from only one side

examples.en: We found a one-sided limit by following only the part of the graph left of zero.
examples.zh: 我们只沿零左侧的曲线观察，求出一个「单侧极限」。

examples.en: The exercise asks for a one-sided limit at the endpoint of the domain.
examples.zh: 这道题要求求出定义域端点处的「单侧极限」。

words.enDefinition: Value approached as inputs smaller than the target get closer to it

examples.en: The left-hand limit is two because the curve approaches that height from the left.
examples.zh: 「左极限」是二，因为图像从左侧趋近这个高度。

examples.en: We used only inputs smaller than three to estimate the left-hand limit at three.
examples.zh: 我们只用了小于三的输入来估算三处的「左极限」。

collocations: read the left-hand limit from a graph

words.enDefinition: Value approached as inputs larger than the target get closer to it

examples.en: The right-hand limit at the step is five in our example, while the left side approaches two.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，阶梯跳变处的「右极限」是五，左侧则趋近二。

examples.en: We traced the branch with larger input values to find the right-hand limit.
examples.zh: 我们追踪输入值较大的一侧分支来求「右极限」。

collocations: read the right-hand limit from a graph

words.enDefinition: Common value approached as inputs come toward a point from either side

examples.en: The two-sided limit exists because both branches approach the same height near zero.
examples.zh: 由于两条分支在零附近都趋近同一高度，「双侧极限」存在。

examples.en: The two-sided limit fails to exist where the two sides approach different heights.
examples.zh: 两侧趋近不同高度的地方，「双侧极限」不存在。

words.enDefinition: Statement that no single limiting value is approached under the stated convention

examples.en: We concluded that the limit does not exist because the outputs kept oscillating near zero.
examples.zh: 我们得出「极限不存在」的结论，因为函数值在零附近不断振荡。

examples.en: Where the branches approach different heights, the limit does not exist even if the function value is defined.
examples.zh: 两条分支趋近不同高度时，即使函数值有定义，「极限不存在」。

collocations: show that the limit does not exist
conclude that the limit does not exist
explain why the limit does not exist

words.enDefinition: A limit of positive or negative infinity, meaning the outputs eventually exceed every bound in the corresponding direction

examples.en: The graph shows an infinite limit as the input approaches zero from above.
examples.zh: 输入从正侧趋近零时，图像显示出「无穷极限」。

examples.en: We used an infinite limit to describe a branch that drops without bound near three.
examples.zh: 我们用「无穷极限」来描述在三附近无界下降的曲线分支。

words.enDefinition: Behavior of outputs as the input grows without bound in either direction

examples.en: We calculated the limit at infinity to describe what happens as the input becomes very large.
examples.zh: 我们计算了「无穷远处的极限」，描述输入变得很大时函数的表现。

examples.en: The limit at infinity told us which horizontal line the right branch approaches.
examples.zh: 「无穷远处的极限」告诉我们右侧分支趋近哪条水平线。

words.enDefinition: Interval around a point with the center point itself left out

examples.en: Our proof uses a punctured neighborhood so the value at the center is irrelevant.
examples.zh: 我们的证明采用「去心邻域」，因此中心点处的值无关紧要。

examples.en: The denominator stays nonzero throughout a sufficiently small punctured neighborhood of the target point.
examples.zh: 在目标点足够小的「去心邻域」内，分母始终非零。

words.enDefinition: Formal limit criterion controlling output error by choosing a sufficiently small input tolerance

examples.en: We used the epsilon-delta definition to prove what the table had merely suggested.
examples.zh: 我们用「ε–δ 定义」证明了表格仅能提示的结论。

examples.en: In the epsilon-delta definition, we choose an input tolerance for each requested output tolerance.
examples.zh: 在「ε–δ 定义」中，我们针对每个给定的输出误差选取输入容差。

words.expression: choose delta in terms of epsilon
words.lemma: choose delta in terms of epsilon
words.enDefinition: Select an input tolerance depending on the requested bound for output error
acceptedEnVariants: choose delta in terms of epsilon

examples.en: The proof asks us to choose delta in terms of epsilon before checking the bound on the function.
examples.zh: 证明要求我们先「用ε确定δ」，再检验函数值的误差界。

examples.en: We can choose delta in terms of epsilon after bounding the output error by twice the input error.
examples.zh: 将输出误差限制在输入误差两倍以内后，我们就可以「用ε确定δ」。

collocations: choose delta in terms of epsilon explicitly
need to choose delta in terms of epsilon
show how to choose delta in terms of epsilon

words.enDefinition: Rules combining existing limits to evaluate sums, products, and other expressions

examples.en: We applied the limit laws once we knew both terms approached finite values.
examples.zh: 得知两项都趋近有限值后，我们应用了「极限定律」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which limit laws justified taking the two limits separately.
examples.zh: 老师问，分别求这两个极限的步骤依据的是哪些「极限定律」。

collocations: justify a step using limit laws
verify the conditions for limit laws

words.enDefinition: Rule dividing existing limits when the denominator's limit is nonzero

examples.en: We used the quotient law for limits after verifying that the denominator approached a nonzero number.
examples.zh: 确认分母趋近一个非零数后，我们用了「极限的商法则」。

examples.en: The quotient law for limits cannot justify dividing by zero in this example calculation.
examples.zh: 在这道计算示例中，「极限的商法则」不能作为除以零的依据。

collocations: apply the quotient law for limits
use the quotient law for limits
conditions for the quotient law for limits

words.enDefinition: Evaluating a limit by plugging in the approach point when continuity permits

examples.en: For this polynomial, direct substitution gives the limit at the marked input.
examples.zh: 对于这个多项式，「直接代入」就能求出标记输入值处的极限。

examples.en: We simplified the fraction before using direct substitution at the excluded input.
examples.zh: 我们先化简分式，再把原式排除的输入值「直接代入」化简后的式子。

collocations: direct substitution into a continuous function

words.enDefinition: Result giving a limit when lower and upper bounds approach the same value

examples.en: We applied the squeeze theorem after finding two bounds that both approach zero.
examples.zh: 找到了两个都趋近零的界后，我们用了「夹逼定理」。

examples.en: The worksheet uses the squeeze theorem on a product with an oscillating factor.
examples.zh: 习题对一个含振荡因子的乘积使用了「夹逼定理」。

collocations: prove a limit using the squeeze theorem

words.enDefinition: Combination of limit behaviors insufficient by itself to determine the result

examples.en: The fraction produced an indeterminate form, so we simplified it before taking the limit.
examples.zh: 分式呈现「未定式」，所以我们先化简，再求极限。

examples.en: We identified the indeterminate form before deciding whether a derivative rule would apply.
examples.zh: 我们先确定了「未定式」，再判断是否适用求导规则。

words.enDefinition: Quotient limit pattern in which numerator and denominator both approach zero

examples.en: The zero over zero form disappeared after we canceled a common factor outside the excluded point.
examples.zh: 我们在排除点之外约去公因式后，「零比零未定式」消失了。

examples.en: We recognized a zero over zero form because both expressions vanished at the approach point.
examples.zh: 因为两个式子在趋近的点都为零，我们判断这是「零比零未定式」。

collocations: identify a zero over zero form
reduce to a zero over zero form
resolve a zero over zero form

words.enDefinition: Quotient limit pattern in which both terms diverge to positive or negative infinity

examples.en: We handled an infinity over infinity form by dividing both expressions by the highest power present.
examples.zh: 我们用最高次幂同除两个式子，处理了「无穷比无穷未定式」。

examples.en: The infinity over infinity form tells us to look more closely at the relative growth rates.
examples.zh: 「无穷比无穷未定式」提示我们进一步观察两边增长速度的相对大小。

collocations: identify an infinity over infinity form
resolve an infinity over infinity form
reduce to an infinity over infinity form

words.enDefinition: Remove a shared nonzero factor from both numerator and denominator

examples.en: We can cancel a common factor to simplify the quotient everywhere except the excluded point.
examples.zh: 我们可以「约去公因式」，将排除点之外的商进行化简。

examples.en: Before we cancel a common factor, we check where that factor has the value zero.
examples.zh: 在「约去公因式」之前，我们先检查因式在哪些点为零。

collocations: cancel a common factor in a quotient
cancel a common factor before evaluating a limit
cancel a common factor from numerator and denominator

words.enDefinition: Remove a radical from the top of a quotient using algebra

examples.en: We chose to rationalize the numerator because the difference of square roots was difficult to evaluate.
examples.zh: 由于平方根之差难以计算，我们选择了「分子有理化」。

examples.en: To rationalize the numerator, we multiplied the fraction by one written with the conjugate expression.
examples.zh: 为了「分子有理化」，我们把分式乘以用共轭式写成的一。

collocations: rationalize the numerator using its conjugate
rationalize the numerator of the quotient

words.enDefinition: A function continuous at each point of its domain, taking limits along inputs within that domain

examples.en: The exercise starts with a continuous function whose graph has no gaps on the interval.
examples.zh: 习题从一个在该区间内图像没有断开的「连续函数」讲起。

examples.en: We used direct substitution because the formula gives a continuous function near the marked input.
examples.zh: 因为公式在标记的输入值附近给出一个「连续函数」，我们使用了直接代入。

collocations: evaluate a continuous function at a point

words.enDefinition: Property that a function has a limit equal to its value there

examples.en: To check continuity at a point, we compared the limit with the function value at zero.
examples.zh: 为了检查「点处连续性」，我们比较了极限和零处的函数值。

examples.en: The example fails continuity at a point because the two branches approach different values there.
examples.zh: 示例不满足「点处连续性」，因为两条分支在该点趋近不同的值。

collocations: condition for continuity at a point

words.enDefinition: Equality of a function's one-sided limit and value at the point

examples.en: We checked one-sided continuity because the square root was defined only to the right.
examples.zh: 平方根在该点右侧才有定义，因此我们检查了「单侧连续性」。

examples.en: The definition of one-sided continuity helps us handle endpoints that have only one nearby side.
examples.zh: 「单侧连续性」的定义有助于处理只能从一侧趋近的端点。

words.enDefinition: Continuity inside an interval and inward one-sided continuity at both endpoints

examples.en: We verified continuity on a closed interval before using the theorem to locate a zero.
examples.zh: 我们验证了「闭区间上的连续性」，再用定理定位零点。

examples.en: The definition of continuity on a closed interval uses limits from inside the interval at each endpoint.
examples.zh: 「闭区间上的连续性」的定义在各端点取从区间内部趋近的极限。

collocations: check continuity on a closed interval
assume continuity on a closed interval
condition of continuity on a closed interval

words.enDefinition: Input where a function fails to be continuous under the stated convention

examples.en: We marked the point of discontinuity where the graph jumps from one height to another.
examples.zh: 我们标出了图像从一个高度跳到另一个高度的「间断点」。

examples.en: The student located a point of discontinuity by comparing the closed dot with the approached value.
examples.zh: 这名学生比较实心点的值和函数趋近的值，找到了「间断点」。

words.enDefinition: Break that can be repaired by assigning the function its finite limiting value

examples.en: The open circle indicates a removable discontinuity because both sides approach the same value.
examples.zh: 空心圆表示「可去间断」，因为两侧都趋近相同的值。

examples.en: We fixed the removable discontinuity by giving the function the missing value at zero.
examples.zh: 我们为函数补上零处缺失的值，修复了「可去间断」。

collocations: remove a removable discontinuity by redefining the function

words.enDefinition: Break where the two finite one-sided limits are different

examples.en: Our step graph has a jump discontinuity where the two flat segments end.
examples.zh: 我们的阶梯图在两条水平线段衔接处有一个「跳跃间断」。

examples.en: Changing just the value at the marked point cannot repair a jump discontinuity.
examples.zh: 仅改变标记点的值无法修复「跳跃间断」。

words.enDefinition: Break where function values grow without bound from at least one side

examples.en: The graph has an infinite discontinuity because its right branch climbs without bound.
examples.zh: 该图像有一个「无穷间断」，因为右侧分支无界上升。

examples.en: We marked an infinite discontinuity where changing a single function value would not help.
examples.zh: 我们标出了一个「无穷间断」，只改某一点的函数值无法修复它。

words.enDefinition: Break where persistent oscillation prevents a limiting value at the point

examples.en: The graph shows an oscillatory discontinuity because the oscillations never settle near zero.
examples.zh: 图像展示了「振荡间断」，因为零附近的振荡始终没有平息。

examples.en: We distinguished an oscillatory discontinuity from a jump by looking for separate one-sided limits.
examples.zh: 我们观察左右极限是否各自存在，以区分「振荡间断」和跳跃间断。

words.enDefinition: Function given by different formulas on different parts of its domain

examples.en: We graphed a piecewise-defined function that uses a different formula on each side of zero.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个「分段定义的函数」的图像，该函数在零的两侧采用不同公式。

examples.en: At the boundary of a piecewise-defined function, check which formula includes the endpoint.
examples.zh: 在「分段定义的函数」的分段边界，要查看哪个公式包含这个端点。

words.enDefinition: Function extending the original domain while preserving continuity and existing values

examples.en: We found a continuous extension by filling the hole with the limiting value.
examples.zh: 我们用极限值填补空缺，求得了「连续延拓」。

examples.en: A continuous extension exists here because the original formula approaches one finite value.
examples.zh: 这里存在「连续延拓」，因为原公式趋近一个确定的有限值。

words.enDefinition: Result that a continuous function attains every value between two endpoint outputs

examples.en: The intermediate value theorem guarantees a zero between endpoints with opposite signs in this example.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，「介值定理」保证两个端点处函数值异号时，它们之间有零点。

examples.en: We used the intermediate value theorem only after checking continuity on the whole interval.
examples.zh: 我们先检查函数在整个区间上连续，再使用「介值定理」。

collocations: hypotheses of the intermediate value theorem
use the intermediate value theorem to locate a root

words.enDefinition: Locating a root within an interval using opposite signs and continuity

examples.en: We used root bracketing to show that a zero lay between the two endpoints.
examples.zh: 我们用「区间夹逼求根」，确定两个端点之间至少有一个零点。

examples.en: The root bracketing step came before we tried to estimate the exact root.
examples.zh: 我们先做了「区间夹逼求根」，再尝试估计零点的具体数值。

words.enDefinition: Root finding by repeatedly halving an interval and retaining a sign change

examples.en: The bisection method retained the half with opposite signs at its new endpoints.
examples.zh: 「二分求根法」保留了两个新端点异号的那一半区间。

examples.en: We used the bisection method on a continuous function after checking the endpoint signs.
examples.zh: 检查端点函数值的符号后，我们对这个连续函数使用了「二分求根法」。

words.enDefinition: Vertical line approached along a branch whose values diverge to infinity

examples.en: The function has a vertical asymptote where the left branch falls without bound.
examples.zh: 函数左侧分支无界下降的地方有一条「竖直渐近线」。

examples.en: We checked the limit before deciding that the denominator's zero gave a vertical asymptote.
examples.zh: 断定分母为零处存在「竖直渐近线」之前，我们先检查了极限。

words.enDefinition: Horizontal line approached as the input goes to positive or negative infinity

examples.en: Our function crosses its horizontal asymptote before approaching the line again at large inputs.
examples.zh: 我们的函数穿过了「水平渐近线」，在输入很大时又趋近于这条线。

examples.en: We found a horizontal asymptote by taking the limit as the input grew without bound.
examples.zh: 我们求输入无界增大时的极限，据此找到一条「水平渐近线」。

words.enDefinition: Nonhorizontal line whose vertical separation from the function tends to zero at infinity

examples.en: Polynomial division revealed a slant asymptote because the remaining fraction tends to zero.
examples.zh: 由于剩余分式趋于零，多项式除法给出了「斜渐近线」。

examples.en: We drew the slant asymptote to show the behavior of the far right branch.
examples.zh: 我们画出「斜渐近线」，展示图像最右侧分支的走势。

collocations: identify a slant asymptote by division

words.enDefinition: Change in output divided by the corresponding change in input

examples.en: We found the average rate of change in temperature from noon until three in the afternoon.
examples.zh: 我们计算了温度从中午到下午三点的「平均变化率」。

examples.en: The graph lets us compare the average rate of change over two intervals of equal length.
examples.zh: 这张图让我们可以比较两个等长区间上的「平均变化率」。

collocations: calculate the average rate of change
average rate of change over an interval
interpret the average rate of change

words.enDefinition: Rate at a particular input obtained as nearby average rates approach a limit

examples.en: The instantaneous rate of change in water level gives the rate at that exact moment.
examples.zh: 水位的「瞬时变化率」给出了水位在那个时刻的变化速度。

examples.en: We approximated the instantaneous rate of change using readings closer and closer to the selected time.
examples.zh: 我们用时刻越来越接近所选时刻的观测值，近似求出了「瞬时变化率」。

collocations: estimate the instantaneous rate of change
calculate the instantaneous rate of change
interpret the instantaneous rate of change

words.enDefinition: Ratio of a function's output difference to the corresponding input difference

examples.en: We simplified the difference quotient before letting the change in input approach zero.
examples.zh: 我们先化简「差商」，再让输入的变化量趋近零。

examples.en: The difference quotient is undefined when the two input values are exactly the same.
examples.zh: 两个输入值完全相同时，「差商」无定义。

words.enDefinition: Line passing through two distinct points on the graph being studied

examples.en: The slope of the secant line gives the average change between the two inputs.
examples.zh: 「割线」的斜率给出了两个输入值之间的平均变化率。

examples.en: As the points moved together, the secant line approached the tangent in our drawing.
examples.zh: 随着两点靠拢，我们图中的「割线」逐渐趋近切线。

words.enDefinition: Line through a curve point with the curve's local direction there

examples.en: The slope of the tangent line matches the rate at which the graph rises locally.
examples.zh: 「切线」的斜率与图像在该点附近的上升速率相符。

examples.en: We drew the tangent line through the point where the derivative was known.
examples.zh: 我们在已知导数的点处画出了「切线」。

words.enDefinition: Rate of vertical change per horizontal unit along a tangent line

examples.en: We found the slope of the tangent line by evaluating the derivative at the given input.
examples.zh: 我们将给定的输入值代入导数，求得「切线斜率」。

examples.en: The slope of the tangent line is negative at the marked point on our graph.
examples.zh: 我们图中标记点处的「切线斜率」为负。

collocations: find the slope of the tangent line
use the slope of the tangent line
zero slope of the tangent line

words.enDefinition: Line through a point on a curve and perpendicular to its tangent

examples.en: We drew a normal line through the point where the tangent was already marked.
examples.zh: 我们通过已标出切线的点画了一条「法线」。

examples.en: The normal line is vertical here because the tangent is horizontal at the point.
examples.zh: 因为这个点的切线是水平的，所以这里的「法线」是竖直的。

words.enDefinition: Limit of the difference quotient at a specified input if it exists

examples.en: We estimated the derivative at a point using average rates over progressively smaller intervals.
examples.zh: 我们用越来越短的区间上的平均变化率估算「一点处的导数」。

examples.en: The derivative at a point gives a number for the chosen input in this exercise.
examples.zh: 在这道题中，对选定输入求得的「一点处的导数」是一个数。

collocations: calculate a derivative at a point
evaluate the derivative at a point
estimate a derivative at a point

words.enDefinition: Function assigning the derivative value to each input where that value exists

examples.en: The derivative function has a gap at the cusp of the original curve.
examples.zh: 原曲线存在尖点的位置，「导函数」的图像有一处断开。

words.enDefinition: Maximum or minimum value compared with nearby values within the domain

examples.en: The function has a local extremum even though greater values occur farther away.
examples.zh: 尽管更远处还有更大的函数值，该函数仍有一个「局部极值」。

examples.en: We checked points on both sides before declaring a local extremum in the example.
examples.zh: 在例子中，我们检查了两侧的点后，才确定这里取得「局部极值」。

collocations: necessary condition for a local extremum

words.enDefinition: Function value at least as large as all sufficiently nearby values

examples.en: The smaller peak's height is a local maximum even though the next peak is taller.
examples.zh: 虽然下一个峰更高，较小峰的高度仍是一个「局部最大值」。

examples.en: We found a local maximum where the derivative changed from positive to negative.
examples.zh: 我们在导数由正变负的位置找到了「局部最大值」。

words.enDefinition: Function value at most as large as all sufficiently nearby values

examples.en: The graph has a local minimum at the bottom of the small valley.
examples.zh: 图像在较小凹谷的底部有一个「局部最小值」。

examples.en: The nearby values on both sides were higher than the local minimum at the turning point.
examples.zh: 转折处两侧附近的函数值都高于这个「局部最小值」。

words.enDefinition: Maximum or minimum function value over the entire specified domain

examples.en: A local maximum can fail to be an absolute extremum on a larger domain.
examples.zh: 扩大定义域后，局部最大值不一定还是「全局极值」。

examples.en: The exercise asks whether an absolute extremum exists on the open interval shown.
examples.zh: 习题问图示开区间上是否存在「全局极值」。

words.enDefinition: Largest attained function value over the entire domain being considered

examples.en: The absolute maximum occurs at the endpoint even though the derivative never vanishes.
examples.zh: 虽然导数从不为零，函数仍在一个端点取得「全局最大值」。

examples.en: We compared all the candidate values before choosing the absolute maximum for the interval.
examples.zh: 我们比较所有候选函数值，然后选出这个区间上的「全局最大值」。

words.enDefinition: Smallest attained function value over the entire domain being considered

examples.en: Our graph shows that the absolute minimum is attained at two different inputs.
examples.zh: 我们的图显示，函数在两个不同的输入值处都取得「全局最小值」。

examples.en: The absolute minimum disappears on this interval when we remove the left endpoint.
examples.zh: 去掉左端点后，这个区间上的「全局最小值」也就不存在了。

words.enDefinition: Maximum or minimum value attained at an endpoint of the domain considered

examples.en: The increasing function has an endpoint extremum at the right side of the closed interval.
examples.zh: 这个递增函数在闭区间的右端点取得一个「端点极值」。

examples.en: We checked for an endpoint extremum even though there were no interior critical numbers.
examples.zh: 尽管内部没有临界数，我们还是检查了是否存在「端点极值」。

words.enDefinition: Method comparing endpoint and critical values to locate absolute extrema of continuous functions

examples.en: The closed interval method compares the values at both endpoints and all interior critical numbers.
examples.zh: 「闭区间极值法」比较两个端点和所有内部临界数处的函数值。

examples.en: We used the closed interval method after confirming the function was continuous on the interval.
examples.zh: 确认函数在该区间上连续后，我们使用了「闭区间极值法」。

collocations: requirements for the closed interval method

words.enDefinition: Criterion classifying extrema from fixed derivative signs on either side of a point

examples.en: The first derivative test gives a local minimum when the slope changes from negative to positive.
examples.zh: 斜率由负变正时，「一阶导数判别法」给出局部最小值。

examples.en: We used the first derivative test when the derivative did not exist at the corner.
examples.zh: 由于折角处导数不存在，我们用「一阶导数判别法」判断那里是否有极值。

collocations: classify extrema with the first derivative test

words.enDefinition: Criterion using second derivative sign at a stationary point to classify it

examples.en: The second derivative test identified a local maximum because the second derivative was negative there.
examples.zh: 由于该点的二阶导数为负，「二阶导数判别法」判定了一个局部最大值。

examples.en: We learned that the second derivative test is inconclusive when the second derivative equals zero.
examples.zh: 我们学到，二阶导数为零时，「二阶导数判别法」不能给出结论。

collocations: classify a point using the second derivative test

words.enDefinition: Table displaying where an expression is positive, negative, or zero

examples.en: We drew a sign chart for the derivative before classifying the critical numbers.
examples.zh: 我们先列出了导数的「符号表」，再判断各临界数对应的点属于哪一类。

examples.en: The sign chart shows a change from positive to negative at the rightmost zero.
examples.zh: 「符号表」显示，在最右侧的零点，导数由正变负。

collocations: mark zeros on a sign chart

words.enDefinition: Function giving a larger output for every larger input in its domain

examples.en: Our example has a strictly increasing function whose derivative still vanishes at one point.
examples.zh: 我们示例里的「严格递增函数」，其导数仍然在一点处为零。

examples.en: We showed that the strictly increasing function takes each output value at most once.
examples.zh: 我们证明了「严格递增函数」的每个输出值至多对应一个输入。

collocations: inverse of a strictly increasing function

words.enDefinition: Function giving a smaller output for every larger input in its domain

examples.en: We used the negative slope everywhere to establish a strictly decreasing function on the interval.
examples.zh: 我们根据处处为负的斜率，证明它在区间上是「严格递减函数」。

examples.en: The strictly decreasing function in the example takes its largest value at the left endpoint.
examples.zh: 示例中的「严格递减函数」在左端点取得最大值。

collocations: inverse of a strictly decreasing function

words.enDefinition: Function whose output never gets smaller as the input increases

examples.en: The graph can describe a nondecreasing function even with a flat section in the middle.
examples.zh: 即使中间有一段水平线，图像仍可以对应一个「非递减函数」。

examples.en: We verified that the nondecreasing function never went down as we moved rightward.
examples.zh: 我们确认向右移动时，「非递减函数」的图像始终没有下降。

collocations: a nondecreasing function with flat sections

words.enDefinition: Interval on which function values grow as the inputs become larger

examples.en: We marked the interval of increase where the derivative is positive in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，我们标出导数为正处的「递增区间」。

examples.en: The exercise asks for the interval of increase between two points where the slope vanishes.
examples.zh: 习题要求求出两个斜率为零的点之间的「递增区间」。

words.enDefinition: Interval on which function values fall as the inputs become larger

examples.en: The interval of decrease ends where the graph reaches the bottom of the valley.
examples.zh: 在图像到达谷底的地方，「递减区间」结束。

examples.en: We identified an interval of decrease by checking the derivative between two consecutive zeros.
examples.zh: 我们检查了相邻两个零点之间的导数，确定了一个「递减区间」。

words.enDefinition: Curving so that chords lie above the graph, as when the derivative is nondecreasing on the interval

examples.en: The graph is concave up where its tangent slopes increase from left to right.
examples.zh: 在切线斜率从左到右逐渐增大的位置，图像「向上凹」。

examples.en: We shaded the part that was concave up even though the function was decreasing.
examples.zh: 虽然函数正在递减，我们仍给「向上凹」的部分涂了阴影。

collocations: determine where a curve is concave up

words.enDefinition: Curving so that chords lie below the graph, as when the derivative is nonincreasing on the interval

examples.en: The curve is concave down near the peak because the slopes are decreasing there.
examples.zh: 在峰顶附近斜率逐渐减小，因此曲线在这里「向下凹」。

examples.en: The derivative test shows that the graph stays concave down after the marked point.
examples.zh: 导数检验表明，图像在标记点之后仍然「向下凹」。

collocations: determine where a curve is concave down

words.enDefinition: Plot showing how the original function's slope depends on the input

examples.en: The graph of the derivative lies below the horizontal axis wherever the original slope is negative.
examples.zh: 原函数图像切线斜率为负的位置，「导函数图像」位于横轴下方。

examples.en: We used the graph of the derivative to identify where the original tangent lines were horizontal.
examples.zh: 我们用「导函数图像」找出原曲线切线为水平的位置。

collocations: draw the graph of the derivative
interpret the graph of the derivative
use the graph of the derivative

words.enDefinition: Point on a curve across which its concavity changes direction

examples.en: The inflection point marks the change from bending upward to bending downward here.
examples.zh: 这里的「拐点」标记了由向上弯曲转为向下弯曲的位置。

examples.en: A zero second derivative alone does not establish an inflection point in this exercise.
examples.zh: 在这道题中，仅凭二阶导数为零并不能确定存在「拐点」。

words.enDefinition: Task of finding the best value of a quantity under specified restrictions

examples.en: The optimization problem asks which rectangle has the largest area for a fixed perimeter.
examples.zh: 这个「优化问题」问的是，在周长固定时哪种长方形面积最大。

examples.en: We stated the optimization problem in words before writing it as a function.
examples.zh: 我们先用文字陈述「优化问题」，再把要优化的量写成函数。

words.enDefinition: Function whose value is to be maximized or minimized in a problem

examples.en: The objective function gives the area of the rectangle as its width changes.
examples.zh: 「目标函数」给出长方形面积随宽度变化的情况。

examples.en: We differentiated the objective function after expressing it in just one variable.
examples.zh: 我们先把「目标函数」写成只含一个变量的式子，再对它求导。

words.enDefinition: Equality restricting how the variables in a problem can vary together

examples.en: The constraint equation relates width and length because the total perimeter is fixed.
examples.zh: 总周长固定，所以「约束方程」把宽度与长度联系起来。

examples.en: We obtained a formula for the height by rearranging the constraint equation.
examples.zh: 我们整理「约束方程」后，得到了高度的表达式。

collocations: solve the constraint equation for one variable

words.enDefinition: Interval of input values satisfying the restrictions of a single-variable problem

examples.en: The feasible interval excludes widths that would give the box a negative height.
examples.zh: 「可行区间」排除了会使盒子高度为负的宽度。

examples.en: We determined the feasible interval before looking for a zero of the derivative.
examples.zh: 我们先确定了「可行区间」，再寻找导数的零点。

collocations: restrict the variable to a feasible interval
check endpoints of the feasible interval

words.enDefinition: Substitute a relation to rewrite an expression using fewer independent variables

examples.en: We used the perimeter condition to eliminate a variable before differentiating the area function.
examples.zh: 我们利用周长条件「消去一个变量」，再对面积函数求导。

examples.en: To eliminate a variable, the worksheet solves the height equation and substitutes the result elsewhere.
examples.zh: 为了「消去一个变量」，习题先解出高度，再把结果代入另一个式子。

collocations: eliminate a variable using the constraint
eliminate a variable from the objective

words.enDefinition: Find the largest attained output over the relevant set of inputs

examples.en: To maximize a function on a closed interval, include the two endpoint values in the comparison.
examples.zh: 在闭区间上「求函数的最大值」时，要把两个端点的值也纳入比较。

examples.en: The exercise shows how to maximize a function when there are two interior critical points.
examples.zh: 习题演示了有两个内部临界点时如何「求函数的最大值」。

collocations: maximize a function on an interval
maximize a function subject to a constraint
use derivatives to maximize a function

words.enDefinition: Find the smallest attained output over the relevant set of inputs

examples.en: We needed to minimize a function to find the smallest possible surface area for the box.
examples.zh: 我们需要「求函数的最小值」，从而找到盒子可能具有的最小表面积。

examples.en: To minimize a function, compare the outputs at all candidates that satisfy the given restrictions.
examples.zh: 「求函数的最小值」时，要比较所有满足给定约束的候选点对应的函数值。

collocations: minimize a function on an interval
minimize a function subject to a constraint
use derivatives to minimize a function

words.enDefinition: Iterative root-finding method replacing a function locally with its tangent line

examples.en: We used Newton's method to approximate a zero without solving the equation exactly.
examples.zh: 我们用「牛顿迭代法」近似求出一个零点，省去了方程的精确求解。

examples.en: The tutor showed how Newton's method can fail when the initial slope is zero.
examples.zh: 老师说明了初始点处斜率为零时，「牛顿迭代法」为什么可能失效。

collocations: start Newton's method from an initial guess

words.enDefinition: Update from the current input to where its tangent crosses the axis

examples.en: After one Newton step, the new input was closer to the root in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，执行「牛顿迭代的一步」后，新的输入值更接近零点。

examples.en: The Newton step uses the function value and derivative at the current estimate.
examples.zh: 「牛顿迭代的一步」需要当前估计值处的函数值和导数。

words.enDefinition: Starting estimate supplied before repeatedly applying a numerical update method

examples.en: We chose an initial guess near the apparent root shown on the graph.
examples.zh: 我们在图示的可能零点附近选取了一个「初始猜测值」。

examples.en: A different initial guess led the method to another zero in the example.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，另一个「初始猜测值」使该方法找到了不同的零点。

words.enDefinition: Drawing a qualitative graph using key features inferred from an expression

examples.en: We used curve sketching to combine information about slopes, concavity, and the endpoints.
examples.zh: 我们通过「曲线描绘」综合了关于斜率、凹凸性和端点的信息。

examples.en: The curve sketching exercise asks us to mark the vertical asymptote before drawing branches.
examples.zh: 这道「曲线描绘」练习要求我们先标出竖直渐近线，再绘制各分支。
